prompt: ISO 14001 treats continual improvement as its own requirement, separate from fixing individual problems. What exactly is supposed to continually improve, and under which clause?
response:
In ISO 14001:2015, continual improvement is indeed a distinct requirement with specific scope.

## What Must Continually Improve

**Clause 10.3** requires continual improvement of the **environmental management system** itself — not just fixing individual nonconformities (which is addressed separately in 10.2).

The standard specifies improvement in:
- **Suitability** — remains appropriate to context
- **Adequacy** — has the right elements
- **Effectiveness** — achieves intended results

## The Distinction

| Activity | Clause | Focus |
|----------|--------|-------|
| Correcting nonconformities | 10.2 | Specific problems, incidents, failures |
| Continual improvement | 10.3 | The EMS as a whole, over time |

## What This Looks Like in Practice

Continual improvement under 10.3 involves:
- Enhancing environmental performance (though note: **Clause 6.2.1** separately requires continual improvement *of* environmental performance)
- Refining processes based on monitoring, audits, management review
- Advancing maturity of the EMS — better integration, more proactive approaches, improved engagement

## Key Relationship

Clause 6.2.1 (environmental objectives) and 10.3 work together: objectives drive performance improvement, while 10.3 ensures the *system* evolves to support ever-better performance.

The 2015 revision strengthened this by embedding improvement throughout (risk-based thinking, lifecycle perspective) rather than treating it as an add-on.
